# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. GBA Unpredictable Things Forward Most of the below is caused by 'traces' from previous operations which have used the databus. No promises that the results are stable on all current or future GBA models, and/or under all temperature and interference circumstances. Also, below specifies 32bit data accesses only. When reading units less than 32bit, data is rotated depending on the alignment of the originally specified address, and 8bit or 16bit are then isolated from the 32bit value as usually. Reading from BIOS Memory (00000000-00003FFF) The BIOS memory is protected against reading, the GBA allows to read opcodes or data only if the program counter is located inside of the BIOS area. If the program counter is not in the BIOS area, reading will return the most recent successfully fetched BIOS opcode (eg. the opcode at [00DCh+8] after startup and SoftReset, the opcode at [0134h+8] during IRQ execution, and opcode at [013Ch+8] after IRQ execution, and opcode at [0188h+8] after SWI execution). Reading from Unused Memory (00004000-01FFFFFF,10000000-FFFFFFFF) Accessing unused memory at 00004000h-01FFFFFFh, and 10000000h-FFFFFFFFh (and 02000000h-03FFFFFFh when RAM is disabled via Port 4000800h) returns the recently pre-fetched opcode. For ARM code this is simply: WORD = [$+8] For THUMB code the result consists of two 16bit fragments and depends on the address area and alignment where the opcode was stored. For THUMB code in Main RAM, Palette Memory, VRAM, and Cartridge ROM this is: LSW = [$+4], MSW = [$+4] For THUMB code in BIOS or OAM (and in 32K-WRAM on Original-NDS (in GBA mode)): LSW = [$+4], MSW = [$+6] ;for opcodes at 4-byte aligned locations LSW = [$+2], MSW = [$+4] ;for opcodes at non-4-byte aligned locations For THUMB code in 32K-WRAM on GBA, GBA SP, GBA Micro, NDS-Lite (but not NDS): LSW = [$+4], MSW = OldHI ;for opcodes at 4-byte aligned locations LSW = OldLO, MSW = [$+4] ;for opcodes at non-4-byte aligned locations Whereas OldLO/OldHI are usually: OldLO=[$+2], OldHI=[$+2] Unless the previous opcode's prefetch was overwritten; that can happen if the previous opcode was itself an LDR opcode, ie. if it was itself reading data: OldLO=LSW(data), OldHI=MSW(data) Theoretically, this might also change if a DMA transfer occurs. Note: Additionally, as usually, the 32bit data value will be rotated if the data address wasn't 4-byte aligned, and the upper bits of the 32bit value will be masked in case of LDRB/LDRH reads. Note: The opcode prefetch is caused by the prefetch pipeline in the CPU itself, not by the external gamepak prefetch, ie. it works for code in ROM and RAM as well. Reading from Unused or Write-Only I/O Ports Works like above Unused Memory when the entire 32bit memory fragment is Unused (eg. 0E0h) and/or Write-Only (eg. DMA0SAD). And otherwise, returns zero if the lower 16bit fragment is readable (eg. 04Ch=MOSAIC, 04Eh=NOTUSED/ZERO). Reading from GamePak ROM when no Cartridge is inserted Because Gamepak uses the same signal-lines for both 16bit data and for lower 16bit halfword address, the entire gamepak ROM area is effectively filled by incrementing 16bit values (Address/2 AND FFFFh). Memory Mirrors Most internal memory is mirrored across the whole 24bit/16MB address space in which it is located: Slow On-board RAM at 2XXXXXX, Fast On-Chip RAM at 3XXXXXXh, Palette RAM at 5XXXXXXh, VRAM at 6XXXXXXh, and OAM at 7XXXXXXh. Even though VRAM is sized 96K (64K+32K), it is repeated in steps of 128K (64K+32K+32K, the two 32K blocks itself being mirrors of each other). BIOS ROM, Normal ROM Cartridges, and I/O area are NOT mirrored, the only exception is the undocumented I/O port at 4000800h (repeated each 64K). The 64K SRAM area is mirrored across the whole 32MB area at E000000h-FFFFFFFh, also, inside of the 64K SRAM field, 32K SRAM chips are repeated twice. Writing 8bit Data to Video Memory Video Memory (BG, OBJ, OAM, Palette) can be written to in 16bit and 32bit units only. Attempts to write 8bit data (by STRB opcode) won't work: Writes to OBJ (6010000h-6017FFFh) (or 6014000h-6017FFFh in Bitmap mode) and to OAM (7000000h-70003FFh) are ignored, the memory content remains unchanged. Writes to BG (6000000h-600FFFFh) (or 6000000h-6013FFFh in Bitmap mode) and to Palette (5000000h-50003FFh) are writing the new 8bit value to BOTH upper and lower 8bits of the addressed halfword, ie. "[addr AND NOT 1]=data*101h". Using Invalid Tile Numbers In Text mode, large tile numbers (combined with a non-zero character base setting in BGnCNT register) may exceed the available 64K of BG VRAM. On GBA and GBA SP, such invalid tiles are displayed as if the character data is filled by the 16bit BG Map entry value (ie. as vertically striped tiles). Above applies only if there is only one BG layer enabled, with two or more layers, things are getting much more complicated: tile-data is then somehow derived from the other layers, depending on their priority order and scrolling offsets. On NDS (in GBA mode), such invalid tiles are displayed as if the character data is zero-filled (ie. as invisible/transparent tiles). Accessing SRAM Area by 16bit/32bit Reading retrieves 8bit value from specified address, multiplied by 0101h (LDRH) or by 01010101h (LDR). Writing changes the 8bit value at the specified address only, being set to LSB of (source_data ROR (address*8)). NDS Reference Overview DS Technical Data DS I/O Maps 453:4000800h).

content.text:
I found no blockers, but two of the new behaviours don't work as intended, so this needs changes before it merges. `cargo test` passes (75 tests) and the wasm release build succeeds at 74e9152. I didn't run `grade-subset.sh` because the main problem below would make those scores misleading.

To run the tests I briefly checked out 74e9152 in the main checkout. `main` was already at that commit, and I switched back to `main` afterwards, so nothing changed.

All findings are in `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/bus.rs` or `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/io.rs`:

- `src/bus.rs:270`: [major] Nothing outside the tests ever calls `note_instruction_fetch`; `grep` finds no caller under `src/cpu`. So in a real run `executing_address` stays 0. Two results follow:
  - BIOS read protection never applies, because the CPU always looks like it is inside the BIOS.
  - Every open-bus read (unused memory and write-only or unused IO) returns the BIOS word at 0x8 instead of the prefetched opcode at `[$+8]`. Before this change these reads returned 0; now they return a different wrong value.
  - Fix: have the CPU call this hook once per executed instruction, passing that instruction's own address rather than the fetch address `$+8`/`$+4`. That is a contract change for the CPU owner, so put it in NOTES.md or wire it before merging.
- `src/io.rs:111` with `src/bus.rs:452`: [major] For unmapped IO (0x04000400 and up, apart from the 0x800 mirrors), `io_offset` returns 0xFFFFFFFF. After `offset & !1`, the expression `offset & 2` is always 2. So 8/16-bit reads at even halfword addresses get the high half of the open-bus word instead of the low half. Fix: pick the half from the original bus address (`address & 2`), not the sentinel offset. Add a test that does a `read16` at 0x04000400.
- `src/io.rs:105`: [major] This disagrees with gbatek's own example in "Reading from Unused or Write-Only I/O Ports". gbatek says the fragment at 04Ch (MOSAIC) / 04Eh (unused) reads as zero. In this code both halves count as unreadable, so 0x4C returns open bus. The same probably applies to BLDY at 0x54/0x56. Fix: follow gbatek's example, for instance by marking 0x04C as a fragment that reads zero. Add a test.
- `src/bus.rs:208`: [minor] `last_bios_prefetch` starts at 0. gbatek says that after startup it is the opcode at `[00DCh+8]`. If boot skips the BIOS, reads from ROM code return 0 instead of a BIOS opcode. Fix: initialise it from the stub's equivalent post-boot fetch address and note the choice in NOTES.md.
- `src/bus.rs:289`: [minor] The closure name `at` is cryptic. Rename it to something like `halfword_after`.
- `src/bus.rs:83-84`: [minor] The `first_access`/`second_access` closures with literal bit positions are dense. Name the WAITCNT field shifts (e.g. `WS0_FIRST_SHIFT`) or add a comment per field.
- `src/io.rs:100`: [minor] Halfword 0x300 counts as readable, so a byte read of 0x301 (HALTCNT, write-only) returns whatever `irq.rs` stores. Confirm `irq.rs` reads that byte as 0, or special-case it.
- `src/bus.rs:94`: [minor] Bit 5 (256K WRAM enable) and bit 0 (WRAM disable) of 0x4000800 are decoded nowhere and have no `ponytail:` comment saying so. Add the comment.
- `src/gba.rs:105-109`: [minor] The frame-timing test was loosened from an exact per-frame delta to "overshoot < 32". That is justified by the new ROM wait states, but 32 is an arbitrary bound. Base it on the largest possible single-instruction cost or explain the number in the comment.

What checked out:
- **Ownership:** only `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs` and the test in `src/gba.rs` changed, all owned by the integrator.
- **ROM-specific hacks:** none.
- **Originality:** nothing looks copied. Every constant matches a gbatek section: the WAITCNT tables, the 0x0D000020 reset value, the 128K block rule, SRAM byte replication and the ROR on writes, the VRAM byte-write limits, the 64K mirror of 0x800, and the THUMB open-bus cases for BIOS/OAM/IWRAM.
